memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: 'They must abstain from wine and other fermented drink and must not drink vinegar made from wine or other fermented drink. They must not drink grape juice or eat grapes or raisins. As long as they remain under their Nazirite vow, they must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or skins.' - Num 6:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Nazirite's devotion showed itself in very practical, everyday ways. One of them was abstaining from anything that came from the grapevine — no wine, no grapes, not even raisins. This was not because grapes were evil, but because giving them up was a visible, daily reminder of the person's special dedication to God.

Here is a helpful truth: real devotion to God touches the ordinary details of life. It is easy to feel spiritual in a moment of worship or prayer. But the Nazirite's commitment showed up at the dinner table, in daily choices, in small acts of self-denial repeated day after day.

Sometimes we give up good things, not because they are wrong, but because setting them aside helps us focus more fully on God. This is the heart behind practices like fasting. The point is never the food or drink itself; it is the reorienting of the heart toward the Lord.

The New Testament calls us to a similar wholehearted focus — to run our race by throwing off even good things that might slow us down, fixing our eyes on Jesus (Heb 12:1-2). Not everything we give up is sinful; some things we lay aside simply because we want God more.

What "grapes" might God be inviting you to set aside for a season, so that your heart can focus more fully on Him?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does your devotion to God touch the ordinary details of your life?
- Is there a good thing God is inviting you to set aside for a season?
- What helps you keep your focus on the Lord?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help my devotion to reach into the everyday choices of my life. Give me a heart willing to set aside even good things to focus more on You. Amen.
